original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Exact minima of the 916 ordered target pairs diag([a],[b]) with direct coordinate-CNOT cost 10..12 left open by research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-seed18 (its open question 1), in the same two-register formal model M_2(F2[GL_3(F2)]) with 36 paid generators (six coordinate CNOTs x six rank-one idempotents) and free GL_2(F2) mixing.
scope_change_reason: Same card, model and alphabet as the predecessor package; narrowed to the predecessor's own recorded open question (lengths 9, 10 and 11) rather than a new register model.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the bit-new-register-model card: it tests whether heterogeneous targets in a nonabelian address alphabet can share paid work under free scalar mixing. They cannot here, so this alphabet offers no bit-primitive saving; no kappa change.
stop_rule: Radius-5 join (all words of length <= 10) plus the length-11 stage only for the pairs still undecided; stop when every open pair is exact or the engine exceeds about 3 GB / 10 minutes.
evidence: engine.cpp: radius-4 ball reproduces seed18 (663,496 states, 133,207 cosets, table min(9,d(a)+d(b))); radius-5 ball 16,292,362 states, 1,119,282,418 ordered join pairs: 816 direct-10 pairs have min 10, 96 direct-11 and 4 direct-12 pairs have no word <= 10; length-11 stage (562,639,176 images) finds all 96 direct-11 controls and nothing for the 4 direct-12 pairs. verify.py checks all 916 recorded/direct words formally (stdlib) and reruns the engine with --full. engine3.cpp (one extra dirty register, 168 generators): radius-3 ball 2,705,791 states, 450,868,320 streamed distance-4 images; no pair has a word of length <= 7 shorter than d(a)+d(b), restored or ending at any monomial; all direct words of length <= 7 found.
author: Josie Elliston (with Claude Code)
ai_assistance: Substantial: Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code wrote the engine, verifier and README; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does one dirty third register (restored or ending at any monomial) save any paid call at word length 8 or more?
open_questions.why_it_matters: engine3.cpp excludes savings through length 7 (all pairs with direct cost <= 8); a saving at length >= 8 would be the first sharing of heterogeneous targets in this alphabet.
open_questions.first_step: 4+4 join using 64-bit digests plus anchors of the distance-4 layer as a filter, with exact recheck of every candidate.
open_questions.blocked_by: Memory: the three-register distance-4 layer has hundreds of millions of 216-byte states.

open_questions.question: Is there a written invariant proving min = d(a)+d(b) for all pairs, possibly for GL_n(F2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Replaces a computer search and could extend to larger address groups.
open_questions.first_step: Look for a quotient of F2[GL_3(F2)] that separates the two rows' label counts; seed18's natural representation has aliases and fails.

open_questions.question: Independent second implementation of the radius-5 join.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The lower bounds rest on one engine; seed18 corroborates only radius 4.
open_questions.first_step: A faithful-regular-representation or differently keyed join over the 16.3M-state radius-5 ball.
open_questions.blocked_by: Memory and runtime in a stdlib implementation.
